## Key questions about spend management tools


### What is spend management software?


Spend management software gives finance teams a single system to issue company cards, track expenses, enforce budgets, and pay vendors, instead of stitching together separate tools for cards, expense reports, and bill pay. It typically covers company spend more broadly than traditional expense reporting alone — including corporate cards, employee reimbursements, vendor bills, and in some cases procurement and business credit.


Most spend management platforms integrate with existing accounting software or ERP systems to keep the general ledger current without manual data entry. Scope varies by provider: some tools focus tightly on cards and expense automation for small and midsize businesses, while others extend into procurement, sourcing, and multi-entity global operations for larger organizations.


### How does spend management software work?


1. Card and policy setup. Businesses issue physical or virtual company cards to employees or teams, with spend limits, merchant restrictions, and approval rules configured in advance.
2. Real-time spend capture. As employees swipe a card, submit a bill, or file a reimbursement, the platform captures the transaction and, in many cases, uses AI to read and match receipts automatically.
3. Policy enforcement and approvals. Transactions are checked against configured spend policies and routed to the right approver based on amount, department, or category.
4. Reconciliation and sync. Approved transactions sync to the accounting system or ERP, reducing the manual work of matching receipts to statements at month-end.
5. Reporting and optimization. Finance teams use real-time dashboards to monitor spend by department, vendor, or project and adjust budgets and policies going forward.


### What features should you look for in spend management software?


- **Company cards with built-in controls.** Physical and virtual cards with configurable spend limits, merchant category restrictions, and the ability to freeze or cancel a card instantly.
- **AI-powered expense automation.** Receipt capture and matching, auto-categorization, and memo generation that reduce manual data entry.
- **Budget and approval controls.** Configurable budgets by department or project, with automated approval routing and a complete audit trail.
- **Business credit access.** For businesses that need working capital alongside spend controls, credit lines tied to the same card and expense platform.
- **ERP and accounting integrations.** Native two-way sync with your accounting software so reconciliation happens automatically rather than through CSV imports.
- **Global payment support.** For businesses with international vendors or employees, multi-currency cards, local payment rails, and reimbursements in local currency.


### How much does spend management software cost?


Spend management pricing varies by provider and how the cost is structured:


- BILL Spend & Expense is free to use with no monthly charges and no annual fees for cards \[17\].
- Per-user subscriptions with a free tier are offered by Airwallex, starting at $0 per user/month on its Explore plan before scaling to $12 per user/month on Grow \[6\], and by Brex, which starts at $0 per user, per month on Essentials before $12 per user, per month on Premium \[9\].
- Per-report pricing is used by SAP Concur, with published rates around $7 per report on its Base plan and around $11 per report on its Plus plan \[10\].
- Custom, quote-based pricing is used by Coupa \[12\]\[13\], and Rippling Spend \[14\], where costs depend on business needs, user count, or modules selected.


## Benefits of spend management software


Spend management software delivers value beyond simply replacing paper receipts and spreadsheets:


**Faster, cleaner month-end close.** Automated receipt capture and categorization reduce the manual matching work that typically slows down reconciliation. BILL Spend & Expense users surveyed by UserEvidence reported average monthly time savings of 12 hours and average monthly savings of $10,630.* \[1\]


**Real-time visibility into company spend.** Instead of waiting for a monthly expense report cycle, finance leaders can see card transactions, budgets, and vendor payments as they happen, which makes it easier to catch overspending before it compounds.


**Stronger fraud and overspend protection.** Features like per-vendor virtual cards, instant card freezing, and real-time policy checks help prevent vendor overcharges, compromised card numbers, and out-of-policy purchases before they become a bigger problem.


**Fewer manual approvals and less email chasing.** Configurable approval workflows route expenses and bills to the right reviewer automatically, based on amount, department, or category, instead of relying on email threads.


**Better budget accountability.** Assigning budgets to departments or projects, with real-time tracking against those budgets, gives team leads visibility into their own spend and helps prevent surprises at month-end.


*Based on a survey of 127 BILL Spend & Expense users conducted by UserEvidence in March 2022.


## How to choose the right spend management software for your business


Factor How it affects your decision


Business size and entity structure Single-entity SMBs typically need less complexity than multi-entity organizations, which benefit from platforms that apply policies consistently across every entity.


Global payment needs If you pay vendors or reimburse employees internationally, prioritize platforms with multi-currency cards, local payment rails, and reimbursements in local currency.


Card funding model Some corporate cards draw down a credit line based on business financials, while others are debit-based and funded from an existing balance — the right fit depends on whether your business needs working capital or already holds cash reserves.


Policy and approval complexity Businesses with straightforward spend rules may only need basic limits and category restrictions, while organizations with complex, multi-level approval chains should prioritize granular policy engines.


ERP and accounting integration Check that the platform offers native two-way sync with your accounting software, not just CSV import and export, so reconciliation happens automatically.


Team structure Finance-led organizations may prefer a dedicated spend management platform, while businesses that want spend, HR, and IT managed from a single system may prefer a bundled platform.
